title: Carbon monoxide: alarm and poisoning
summary: If the CO alarm sounds: get outside, call 911, stay out. Never use grills, generators or camp stoves indoors.

sources.title: CPSC: Winter Storm May Knock Out Power; CPSC Warns of Deadly Carbon Monoxide and Fire Risks

blocks.text: **If a CO alarm is sounding, or someone feels sick and you suspect CO: GET OUTSIDE NOW and call 911.**

items: **Don't look for the source.** Go outside to fresh air right away. Take everyone, including pets.
**Call 911** (or the fire department) from outside.
Count heads. **Don't go back in** until responders say it is OK.
Don't run any suspect appliance again until a trained technician has fixed it.
If the alarm goes off again within **24 hours** of going back in, leave again, call 911, and have a qualified technician check every fuel-burning appliance.

blocks.text: Poison Help (free, expert advice): **1-800-222-1222**. For collapse, seizure or trouble breathing, call 911.

items: Early: headache, tiredness, dizziness, shortness of breath, upset stomach. It feels like flu **without a fever**.
Worse: confusion, vomiting, loss of coordination, passing out, death.
People who are **asleep or drunk** can die before they feel anything.
Higher risk: babies, older adults, and people with heart disease, anemia or breathing problems.
A portable generator, even in a garage or with doors and windows open
A charcoal or gas grill
A camp stove (butane or propane)
A gas oven, range or dryer to heat your home
A car running in an attached garage, even with the door open
A charcoal fire in a tent, vehicle or house

blocks.text: Keep generators **at least 20 feet** from doors, windows, vents and attached garages.

items: Put battery-powered or battery-backup CO alarms **on every level and outside each sleeping area**. Interconnected alarms are best.
**Fuel stoves, camp heaters and generators all need a working CO alarm.** If power fails, a plug-in alarm needs its battery.
Test alarms monthly. Replace batteries as needed. Replace the whole alarm per the maker's instructions, about every 5 years.
Don't put an alarm in the kitchen or right above a fuel-burning appliance, or where furniture or curtains cover it.
Keep snow clear of outdoor vents for furnaces and dryers.
